questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a class in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'class' keyword is used to declare a class in Java.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the correct entry point method signature for a standard Java console application?
questions.explanation: The standard entry point is 'public static void main(String[] args)'.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primitive data type in Java?
questions.explanation: String is an object/class type, not a primitive type in Java.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the size of an int variable in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, an int is always 32 bits signed integer regardless of the underlying OS.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the default value of a boolean instance variable in Java?
questions.explanation: The default value for boolean instance variables is false.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the correct way to declare a constant variable in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'final' keyword is used in Java to make a variable unmodifiable.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the result of 10 % 3 in Java?
questions.explanation: The '%' operator computes the remainder of integer division, so 10 % 3 = 1.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the value of result after executing: int a = 5; int result = a++ + ++a;
questions.explanation: a++ evaluates to 5 (a becomes 6), ++a increments a to 7 and evaluates to 7. 5 + 7 = 12.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which operator is used for string concatenation in Java?
questions.explanation: The '+' operator is overloaded for string concatenation in Java.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which conditional statement executes code based on multiple possible values of a single primitive variable?
questions.explanation: The 'switch' statement allows multi-way branching based on discrete values.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.explanation: The do-while loop evaluates its condition after executing the loop body.

questions.subject: Java

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used to immediately exit a loop in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'break' statement terminates the execution of the nearest enclosing loop.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword skips the rest of the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next iteration?
questions.explanation: The 'continue' statement skips the remaining statements in the current iteration.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: How do you obtain the number of elements in an array named 'arr'?
questions.explanation: In Java, array length is accessed via the 'length' field, not a method call.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the valid syntax to initialize an array of integers with 3 elements?
questions.explanation: 'int[] arr = {1, 2, 3};' is a valid array literal initialization.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens if you access an array index out of bounds, such as arr[5] on an array of length 5?
questions.explanation: Accessing index 5 on array of size 5 throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at runtime.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Strings in Java are immutable. What does this mean?

options.B: String objects cannot be changed once created.

questions.explanation: Immutability means once a String object is instantiated, its contents cannot be altered.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the result of string equality check: "hello".equals("HELLO")?
questions.explanation: equals() is case-sensitive, so "hello" does not equal "HELLO".

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which String method returns the character at a specific index?
questions.explanation: charAt(int index) returns the char value at the specified index.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the output of "Java".length()?
questions.explanation: The length() method of String returns the count of characters, which is 4 for "Java".

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What keyword is used when a method does not return any value?
questions.explanation: The 'void' return type specifies that a method returns no value.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is method overloading in Java?

options.A: Methods in child class having same signature as parent class
options.B: Multiple methods in the same class with the same name but different parameters

questions.explanation: Overloading occurs when multiple methods in a class share the same name but have different parameter lists.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used to create an instance of a class?
questions.explanation: The 'new' operator allocates memory for a new object.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the purpose of a constructor in Java?
questions.explanation: Constructors are special methods called when an object is instantiated to initialize its state.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Does a class constructor in Java have a return type?
questions.explanation: Constructors do not specify any return type, not even void.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: If no constructor is defined in a Java class, what happens?

options.B: Java provides a default no-argument constructor

questions.explanation: The compiler automatically provides a default no-arg constructor if no constructors are explicitly declared.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which block is used to catch and handle exceptions in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'try-catch' structure is used to enclose exception-prone code and handle caught exceptions.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which block always executes regardless of whether an exception is thrown or caught?
questions.explanation: The 'finally' block is executed after try/catch blocks, whether an exception occurred or not.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which extension is used for compiled Java bytecode files?
questions.explanation: Java source code file compiles into '.class' bytecode files.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which single-line comment syntax is valid in Java?
questions.explanation: '//' is used for single-line comments in Java.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which primitive data type is used to store fractional numbers up to 15-17 decimal digits precision?
questions.explanation: double is a 64-bit IEEE 754 double precision floating-point number.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the output of System.out.println(5 / 2);?
questions.explanation: Integer division in Java truncates the fractional part, yielding 2.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which operator is used to check for logical AND without evaluating the second condition if the first is false?
questions.explanation: '&&' is the short-circuit logical AND operator.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the output of: System.out.println(10 > 5 ? "Yes" : "No");?
questions.explanation: The ternary operator evaluates 10 > 5 (true), returning "Yes".

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the index of the first element in a Java array?
questions.explanation: Java arrays are zero-indexed, starting at 0.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What does the trim() method do on a String?

options.B: Removes leading and trailing white spaces

questions.explanation: trim() removes leading and trailing white space characters.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used by an object to refer to itself?
questions.explanation: The 'this' keyword refers to the current object instance.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used to explicitly throw an exception object in Java?
questions.explanation: 'throw' is used to explicitly throw an exception object.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which keyword is used in a method signature to declare exceptions that might be thrown?
questions.explanation: 'throws' is declared in method signatures for checked exceptions.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Can a method in Java return multiple values directly without wrapping them in an object or array?
questions.explanation: Java methods can return only a single value or object/array reference.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the wrapper class for the primitive type 'int'?
questions.explanation: java.lang.Integer is the wrapper class for the primitive type int.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which access modifier makes a class member visible only within its own class?
questions.explanation: 'private' restricts visibility strictly to within the enclosing class.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which access modifier makes a class member accessible within the same package and subclasses?
questions.explanation: 'protected' allows access within the same package and by child classes.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the result of expression: true || false && false?
questions.explanation: && has higher precedence than ||. false && false is false. true || false is true.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the result of "Java".toUpperCase()?
questions.explanation: toUpperCase() converts all characters in the string to uppercase.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: How do you declare a 2D array of integers in Java?
questions.explanation: 'int[][] arr;' is the standard syntax to declare a 2D array.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which package is automatically imported in every Java program?
questions.explanation: java.lang package is automatically imported by default in Java.
